analysis.title: Builders FirstSource Inc. (BLDR): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: BLDR reported 3Q26 adjusted EPS of $1.36 (including stock-based compensation expense) vs GSe and FactSet consensus of $1.06. A lower tax rate added $0.34 to the result, and revenue added $0.05.
Revenue fell 2% y/y (organic -4%, commodity deflation flat, M&A +2%) vs GSe -5% (organic -6%, commodity deflation flat, M&A +1%).
Adj. EBIT margin of 5.6% was 21bps below GS's model, a $0.06 drag. Interest expense was a $0.02 drag.
Gross margin fell 31bps sequentially to 27.8% vs GSe 27.9%. SG&A margin of 25.3% was worse than GSe 24.9%, attributed to recent acquisitions and higher fuel and insurance expenses.

The full-year adj. EBITDA guide was narrowed but kept at $1.1bn at the midpoint, with gross margin still at 28.0% vs GSe 27.9%. The outlook assumes similar end-market conditions with slightly higher contribution from recent M&A.
The new guide range implies 4Q adj. EBITDA of $246mn at the midpoint vs GSe $211mn and consensus $217mn.

Core organic single-family sales fell 6% vs GSe -8%, on lower starts and reduced content per home. Core multi-family sales rose 2% vs GSe -10%, on higher lumber and lumber sheet goods volumes. R&R/other sales were flat, in line with GSe.
Value-added product mix was ~46% in 3Q, in line with 2Q and below the 50+% target.
Net debt/EBITDA rose to 4.1x from 3.6x in 2Q and 2.3x a year ago. Available liquidity is $1.5bn, and one acquisition was completed in the quarter.
3Q FCF of $76mn missed GSe $453mn, mainly on working capital. The midpoint of the 2026 FCF guide was cut by $25mn to $425mn.
GS keeps a Buy rating and a $77 12-month price target (11.7x Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA) against a $55.88 price, 37.8% upside. Housing demand softened through the summer as mortgage rates reached 7.5%.

Questions for the call: framework for 4Q and 2027 scenarios, competitive pressures, benefits from the shift to BTO and productivity initiatives, multifamily and R&R outlook, fuel costs and margins, SG&A outlook, and uses of cash.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Buy and the $77 target after the 3Q26 print. The EPS beat came mostly from a lower tax rate, and the guide implies 4Q EBITDA above GSe and consensus.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term housing conditions are expected to persist, with single-family starts and content per home lower, while multi-family and R&R held up better than GS forecast.

earnings_insights: BLDR 3Q26 adj. EPS $1.36 reported (including stock-based compensation expense) vs GSe and FactSet consensus est $1.06. Lower tax rate contributed +$0.34, revenue +$0.05, adj. EBIT margin ($0.06), interest expense ($0.02).
3Q26 revenue down 2% y/y reported (organic -4%, commodity deflation flat, M&A +2%) vs GSe -5%.
3Q26 gross margin 27.8% reported vs GSe 27.9%, down 31bps sequentially. SG&A margin 25.3% reported vs GSe 24.9%.
FY26 adj. EBITDA guide narrowed, midpoint $1.1bn maintained, gross margin guide 28.0% vs GSe 27.9%. Implied 4Q adj. EBITDA $246mn at midpoint vs GSe $211mn and consensus est $217mn.
GS estimates: FY26E EPS $0.82, FY27E $1.44, FY28E $2.97. FY25 EPS $4.87. Quarterly EPS GSe: 9/26E $0.57, 12/26E ($0.07), 3/27E ($0.20).
FY26 FCF guide midpoint cut by $25mn to $425mn. 3Q FCF $76mn reported vs GSe $453mn.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Mortgage rates reaching 7.5% decelerated the housing backdrop, weighing on single-family starts and building products demand.

risk_factors: Weaker than expected demand for new single-family homes.
Multi-family starts decline persisting longer than anticipated.
Greater competition if peers seek to gain share.
Higher material prices that cannot be passed through.
